title: Minimal versioned control catalog: control definitions and applicability rules
statement: A control is an attributable, versioned obligation with an applicability rule and a real enforcement point. This catalog defines controls; it is not evidence that any control is enforced. Until a control is linked to independently sourced evidence (plan leaf G-01.2), its assessment is unknown, and unknown never satisfies a control.
reference_form: governance:<control id>@<full commit id of the admitted revision of this file>

authority.note: The Owner is the rule authority: control definitions, applicability and exceptions change only by an Owner policy change. An agent may propose a control or a stricter applicability, never adopt or weaken one.

approval.quote: APPROVED: Admit the governance control catalog

admission.realization: Bootstrap: an Owner sign-off of an exact revision of this file, transcribed verbatim into evidence/bootstrap-log.md by the Overseer, as every Owner policy decision is today. Planned: the protected Gitea policy repository (repo-gitea-policy), where the catalog is promoted by the protected catalog merge of blueprint #sequence-maps governance step 04, which the M-5 reconciliation (2026-11-11) left unchanged. Decision 0012 does not cover catalog admission: the authorization recorder performs no catalog merge and gains no authority over it. No mechanism for that merge is decided.

categories.isolation: Workload isolation: what an agent run can reach.
categories.credentials: Credential separation: which credentials an agent run can hold or read.
categories.ci: Mandatory CI: the required checks that gate a protected merge on the exact commit.
categories.code-review: Independent review of the exact change.
categories.authorization: Owner authorization of a consequential effect.
categories.evidence: Evidence integrity: what a control verdict may rest on.
categories.recovery: Recovery: durable state survives a change, and an unknown outcome is reconciled, never replayed.

boundaries.execution: The execution boundary (blueprint #security, 3): OS, VM and container isolation, the restricted launcher and the credentials an attempt is given.
boundaries.git-ci: The Git and CI boundary (blueprint #security, 4): protected branches, required checks on the current head, merge restrictions and contained CI jobs.
boundaries.effect: The effect boundary (blueprint #security, 5): the Owner's protected authorization of an exact operation and the allowlisted executor that re-checks it.
boundaries.evidence: The evidence boundary (blueprint #security, 6): the independent resolution of evidence for an exact subject, revision and policy version.

exception_classes.prohibited: No exception can be granted: the control is a non-waivable identity or containment invariant.
exception_classes.scoped: A separately authorized, time-bounded exception may let work proceed under stated conditions; it never rewrites the failed or unknown assessment to passed.
exception_classes.unsettled: The accepted records do not settle whether an exception may be granted; until they do, none can be (fail closed). Settled at the leaf named in exception_settled_at.

exception_contract.rule: An exception is bound to one control id, its target, the reason, the residual risk, the compensating measures and an expiry. Only the Owner grants one; an agent may propose one and never grants it. A waiver never overrides physical isolation or unauthorized credential access.

classification_inputs.repository-classification: The classification of the repository the change or operation touches.
classification_inputs.change-surface: What the change touches (for example authentication, secrets, public networking, durable data or an execution boundary).
classification_inputs.target-environment: Where a change or operation takes effect.
classification_inputs.risk: The risk classification of the Work.
classification_inputs.operation-type: Whether the transition is an ordinary engineering change or a consequential effect that needs the Owner's authorization.

profiles.name: Baseline engineering
profiles.obligations: Every attempt: isolated workspace, approved agent/skill digests, outcome/Work lineage. Every PR: protected CI checks, tested commit, review requirements by policy.

profiles.name: Elevated-risk change
profiles.obligations: Add scoped threat analysis, targeted adversarial tests, license/security assessment, enhanced isolation and independent security review when work touches auth, secrets, public networking, durable data or execution boundaries.

profiles.name: Consequential operation
profiles.obligations: Add protected Owner authorization, exact effect digest, privilege-separated execution, data protection/rollback preconditions and independently observed outcome. Non-waivable identity and containment invariants still apply.

resolution.rule: A control profile is resolved deterministically from repository classification, change surface, target environment, risk and operation type. Profiles are additive: baseline always applies, and every profile whose condition holds adds its controls.
resolution.unknown: Unknown classification selects the safer profile or blocks the consequential transition: an input whose value is unknown counts as meeting every condition on it, and a transition whose operation type is unknown is not performed.
resolution.downgrade: An agent may propose stricter checks or ask to resolve uncertainty, but cannot downgrade mandatory controls; trusted checks enforce the mandatory baseline controls even if agents omit them.

controls.title: Workload isolation
controls.purpose: An agent run executes only inside an approved workload profile: no protected mount, administrative socket or unauthorized network is reachable from it, whatever its prompt or instructions say.

subject.scope: Every agent run (one engineering conversation), bound to the execution profile it ran under.

events: every change of an execution profile

enforcement.mechanism: The restricted launcher starts only approved workload profiles and denies protected mounts, administrative sockets and unauthorized networks; the sandbox mount and permission manifest is the guard, not the agent prompt.
The execution guest is the VM boundary against untrusted agents, and its container egress guard refuses every forwarded connection from a container bridge (S-01.4).

controls.failure_effect: Block execution for core boundaries. No exception allowing Owner secret access.

controls.title: Owner credentials out of agent reach
controls.purpose: Agent execution cannot access Owner credentials: an agent run holds only credentials issued for that single attempt and can read no Owner, administrator, executor, management or standing Gitea bot credential; its role's standing bot credential stays on the trusted host and only the dispatcher uses it, on the run's behalf.

subject.scope: Every agent run, with the credentials issued for it and the dispatcher's use of its stage's standing credential on its behalf.

events: every borrowing of a stage's standing bot credential by the dispatcher for a confirmed attempt
every issuance of a credential for a single attempt

enforcement.mechanism: No Owner secrets or host home mounts. The standing Gitea bot credentials stay on the trusted host in the OS credential provider; for a confirmed attempt the dispatcher borrows only the stage's mapped credential into its own in-memory attempt context, uses it there and releases it when the operation ends, which is not Gitea revocation; a standing credential never enters a guest, an agent environment, a container, a conversation, a conversation record or the UI, and records carry fingerprints only. Issuance, rotation and revocation of a standing credential are the Gitea site administrator's, on defined security and lifecycle triggers (suspected exposure, definition revocation, policy revision, expiry, Owner direction), never on routine attempt completion; the dispatcher issues, rotates and revokes none. The per-attempt inference token is issued by the inference broker and revoked at attempt end (decision 0015). Disclosed, not prevented: during bootstrap the Owner's account can read the standing credentials in the credential provider (decision 0013 point 6). Decision 0007 points 4 and 5, amendment 1; decision 0013 point 7.

Each agent role's Gitea identity is a non-administrator Bot account whose token carries the role's narrowest scope; no agent identity holds an Owner, administrator or executor credential (policy/role-tokens.json).

controls.failure_effect: Block execution: a waiver never overrides unauthorized credential access.

controls.title: Code hygiene and tests
controls.purpose: The required lint, format, test, coverage and acceptance-mapping checks run independently against the exact pull-request commit, and a protected merge waits for all of them; absent checks fail closed.

subject.scope: Every revision of a pull request to a protected branch.

enforcement.mechanism: Protected branch rules require the mandatory status checks on the current head, from centrally required workflows that a consuming repository cannot opt out of.
The required Gitea Actions jobs run in a disposable, contained job on the dedicated runner host, against the exact pull-request commit.

controls.failure_effect: Protected merge blocked; corrected revision must be retested.

controls.title: Secrets and vulnerabilities
controls.purpose: The required secret, dependency and SBOM scans run against the exact commit, and their findings are triaged against a published risk policy before a protected merge or a release.

subject.scope: Every revision of a pull request to a protected branch, every release candidate and every dependency change.

enforcement.mechanism: The scans are required status checks of the protected branch; a material finding without a permitted scoped exception keeps the merge blocked.
The pinned scanners run as required jobs in the contained CI job against the exact commit.

controls.failure_effect: Block material findings or request a permitted scoped exception.

controls.title: Independent challenge
controls.purpose: A review independent of the author receives the immutable accepted goal and the exact diff; its approval counts only for the revision it reviewed.

subject.scope: Every pull-request revision whose merge requires a review.

events: every review the protected code-merge policy requires (decided at D-01.2)
every elevated-risk change: an independent security review

enforcement.mechanism: Merge rules require the applicable approvals on the current head and dismiss stale approvals.
The reviewer runs in a session, runner or model and context separate from the builder's, under its own Bot identity, which can submit reviews and cannot merge.

controls.failure_effect: Return to same Work for rework; invalidate review on material revision change.

controls.title: Owner authority
controls.purpose: A consequential effect happens only on the Owner's recorded authorization of the exact operation manifest, merged onto the protected authorization branch, and after the isolated executor has re-checked the exact target and digest.

subject.scope: Each consequential operation: one operation manifest on the protected authorization branch.

enforcement.mechanism: The protected authorization branch: no direct or force push, and only aieh-owner, the Owner's authority identity, is on its merge allowlist (decision 0012 point 3).
Merges only on a fresh Owner decision bound to the exact head and manifest digest, after the fail-closed protection check (decision 0012 points 4 to 6).
Reads the protected ref, merged_by, the trailers and the exact manifest blob; a protected-branch merge without a recorder trailer or receipt is an unrecorded merge (decision 0012 point 10).
A separate OS identity re-checks the current authorized revision, target and digest before acting, and never trusts a webhook payload.

controls.failure_effect: Block effect; stale or missing authorization never inferred from webhook.

controls.title: Evidence integrity
controls.purpose: A control verdict rests only on independently sourced evidence whose source identity, content integrity, subject, freshness and allowed signer or runner are verified; anything that cannot be verified is unknown or stale, never satisfied.

subject.scope: Each evidence reference that a control verdict relies on.

events: each change of an evidence source a verdict relies on

enforcement.mechanism: The independent evidence resolver, keyed by source revision and observed subject, retrieves the native record, verifies subject, revision, hash, source identity and freshness, and leaves missing evidence unknown; it keeps no second evidence or Work database.

controls.failure_effect: Mark unknown/stale rather than asserting pass.

controls.title: Durable state recovery
controls.purpose: A change or operation that can alter durable state (repositories, conversations, Work, Git history, credentials, operational records) proceeds only with a verified recovery option, and an unknown non-idempotent outcome stops for reconciliation and is never replayed.

subject.scope: Each consequential operation, and each change whose change surface includes durable data.

events: each consequential operation (preconditions such as recovery-available, data-compatible and backup-verified)
each change whose change surface is durable data (migration and data-health tests, a backup or recovery condition)

enforcement.mechanism: Checks the manifest's recovery preconditions and the actual target state before acting, persists its receipt, queries the actual target state after a crash and stops on an unknown non-idempotent effect.
A change whose surface is durable data carries migration and data-health checks among the required checks on its exact commit.

controls.failure_effect: Do not perform the change or operation; reconcile/restore when safe; an unknown outcome stays unknown until reconciled.

deferred_controls.title: Approved agent/skill
deferred_controls.reason: Outside the categories this leaf declares. Its definitions are admitted through the agent and skill catalog (governance steps 01 to 05; step 04, the protected catalog merge, is unchanged by M-5 and outside decision 0012).

deferred_controls.title: Intent/acceptance trace
deferred_controls.reason: Outside the categories this leaf declares; the trace it checks is the lineage projection (P-03.2) and the acceptance verdicts.

deferred_controls.title: Artifact and delivery
deferred_controls.reason: Outside the categories this leaf declares, and its subject, a release artifact, has no settled native identity in the lineage schema.

oscal.note: A small local contract shaped so that a later OSCAL catalog export maps field by field; deliberately not claimed to be an OSCAL document, and no mapping to an external standard (such as NIST SSDF) is asserted.

fields.title: control title
fields.category: group id (the category groups the controls)
fields.applicability: part named applicability, with its profiles as props
fields.enforcement: implementation by-components (a component per enforcing principal)
